data.headline: Director of Vocal Division and Choral Activities at Lone Star College-CyFair
data.about:
As a music director and conductor, Dr. Paulo Gomes’ aims to enhance the musicianship of students by expanding their musical, intellectual, and aesthetic experiences in a safe, nurturing, and uncritical environment. He seeks to not only prepare students for careers in music, but also encourage them to develop an appreciation of music as good performers and critical listeners. Dr. Gomes’ musical outlook has been influenced by his mentors: Dr. Ann Howard Jones, Dr. Charles Hausmann, Joseph Flummerfelt, Craig Smith, Dr. Eph Ehly, Dr. Katalin Kiss, Maestro Roberto Duarte, Maestro Sergio Magnani, and Maestro Carlos Alberto Pinto Fonseca.

His teaching philosophy is based on critical thinking and positive learning, in which students recognize and respect the beliefs and practices of others. He executes this philosophy via direct instructional strategies in areas of musical intelligence, bodily intelligence, kinesthetic intelligence, inter and intrapersonal intelligence. Furthermore, by means of differentiated instruction, Dr. Gomes enables diverse students to further develop individual strengths in different areas. 

In a teaching context, Dr. Gomes believes that outreach programs to the academic community, local schools, and general public are vital. He is passionate about finding the most effective way to foster and stimulate musical growth among students both inside and outside the classroom environment. Dr. Gomes strives to create opportunities for interdisciplinary cooperation among visual arts, language arts, theater, and musicians of different backgrounds. 

Dr. Gomes seeks to engage in musical work opportunities that allow him to inspire and empower others. As a music educator he aspires for his students to become like a philosopher-king from Plato’s Allegory of the Cave: that they are “… able to make distinctions between shadows, images, actual objects, and ideas, or the mental conceptions of things, that allow people to make use of objects and to shine.”

experiences.title: Presenter for the Research Poster Session at the 2015 ACDA National Convention.
experiences.subtitle: America Choral Directors Association (ACDA) . undefined
experiences.caption: Feb 2015 - Feb 2015 ·
experiences.metadata: East Lobby of the Salt Palace Convention Center, Salt lake City, Utah

description.text:
Dear Paulo,

On behalf of the ACDA Research and Publications Committee, I am pleased to invite you to present your research, Missa Afro-Brasileira: An Incorporation of Folk and Popular Brazilian Music in the Ordinary Mass, at the 2015 National Conference in Salt Lake City. Congratulations! The Poster Session presentation is scheduled for Wednesday, February 25 from 1:00 pm to 3:30 pm in the East Lobby of the Salt Palace Convention Center. 
Each presenter will also give a brief oral presentation on their findings.Again, congratulations, and please do not hesitate to contact me if you need additional information or clarification. I look forward to meeting you in Salt Lake City.
 
Sincerely,

Richard Waters
Poster Session Coordinator
